Subject: Question on consolidation path — features when stepping down

Hi Nikhil,

Thanks for the deck yesterday — the execs liked the throughput vs feature tradeoff. A couple quick clarifying questions before we build our internal buy-in:

- If we move from the Pro tier to Compact (step-down), which features are guaranteed to remain for 90 days while we migrate? We need to avoid breaking certain privacy hooks.
- Can you confirm the pricing cliff if we drop below 50% committed throughput in the 2nd quarter? Is there a prorated credit or immediate step-change?

We'd also like to see a simple mapping (SKU -> enabled features) so our product team can map dependencies. If you can send a single-sheet matrix, that would be perfect.

Appreciate it — we want to keep this predictable if we take the pilot to org-wide.

Best,
Alison
VP Product, ClearLine AI

Subject: Re: Question on consolidation path — features when stepping down

Hi Alison — thanks for the note. I sketched a concise stepdown approach and attached a one-page SKU matrix (tier-matrix-v1.xlsx). Key points up-front: 

- Grace window: For all Pro->Compact stepdowns initiated with 30 days' notice, we provide a 90-day grace period where feature flags remain enabled (no runtime removals) while teams migrate integrations.
- Pricing tiers: If committed throughput drops below 50% during an annual term, standard behavior is a step-rate adjustment at the next billing cycle unless you exercise a true-up option. Practically we can offer a prorated credit only if the drop is driven by Redwood-side degradation or scheduled maintenance that we own — otherwise it's normative.
- Concessions: For pilots that convert to a 12-month commitment, Sales can offer a one-time onboarding credit or a year-1 discount (guideline in attached concession table). I flagged the most common structures in the matrix.

See the attached matrix for a compact mapping of SKUs -> feature buckets and a second tab with recommended messaging for customer success.

Next steps I propose:
1) Alison: confirm the list of 2–3 features you need guaranteed for 90 days.
2) Ben/Kim: recommend an initial public discount (percent + term) we can present to ClearLine early next week.

Happy to hop on a 30-min call tomorrow if helpful.

Thanks,
Nikhil
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments: tier-matrix-v1.xlsx

Looping in pricing guidance. Nikhil — good framing. A couple tactical notes from quota/product: 

- Discount authority: Field team can offer up to 10% off list for 12-month commitments under $150k ACV. Anything above needs Manager approval (Lauren). For strategic pilots (like ClearLine) we can stretch to 12–15% if they (a) commit to a 12-month contract and (b) accept a 6-month limited feature grandfather (documented in the SOW). See approved_concession_table.pdf attached.
- Credit mechanics: Prefer to offer onboarding credits (one-time) rather than permanent list reductions to preserve future upsell motion. Credits get applied monthly over 3 invoices.
- Messaging: Emphasize the 90-day technical grace + a documented rollback plan (we should include a schedule of feature toggles and owners).

If Legal pushes back on grandfathering, we can pivot to a SWP (service work package) where we guarantee API compatibility for 90 days rather than maintaining the managed feature itself. 

Tell Alison: we can present a firm offer at 10% with a conditional escalation to 15% pending Lauren's sign-off and product commit to the rollback plan.

-Ben
Director, Sales Engineering
